reason: Attacked and not broken. I downloaded the scan the verifier named and read the Author's Preface as searchable text. The sentence stands verbatim: 'If this book be not the exact, the absolute, the strict truth, it has no right to exist.' It sits between 'it is precisely because I hope to be read that I am absolutely sincere' and 'I not only say all the time what I think', exactly as the verifier reported, which rules out a spliced or shortened rendering. The subjunctive is the point of attack and it survives: this translation reads 'If this book be not', not the 'If this book is not' that circulates in quotation sites and in later English versions, so the wording belongs to the named translation and was not smoothed. Translator and year are confirmed from the book and not from a catalogue entry: the title page in the same scan reads 'THE JOURNAL OF MARIE BASHKIRTSEFF. TRANSLATED, WITH AN INTRODUCTION, BY MATHILDE BLIND. WITH TWO PORTRAITS. CASSELL & COMPANY, Limited: LONDON, PARIS & MELBOURNE. 1890.' The heading over the passage reads 'AUTHOR'S PREFACE.', so the locator is right, and the verifier was right not to claim a page, since the preface is in roman numerals the scan renders badly. Attribution is not in dispute and the line is on no misattribution list; it is the author's own preface, not a character's line and not one person reporting another, so no speaker is owed. Scope: first published in French in 1887 and in Blind's English in 1890, a named work by a named author, no scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business or oratory. shipped.js returns shipped [], near [], yearCount 0 for 'marie bashkirtseff', not banned, not at cap, and Bashkirtseff appears in no other month 6 lane. Mechanics: the source line leads with the name, has no dash, no straight double quote, and runs 101 characters; the quotation ends in a full stop and contains no straight quotes. The tag Diary is the form of the work, and a preface to a journal is still the journal. Publishable as it stands. The only observation worth passing on, and it is not a refutation: the note field is empty, and because Blind's is an abridged translation an editor may want a line saying the wording is Blind's 1890 rendering.
